name: Hardware Transceiver Evaluation
description: Security evaluation of hardware radio transceivers embedded in devices. Covers assessment of Bluetooth, Zigbee, LoRa, Sub-GHz, and proprietary radio hardware at the chip and firmware level. Includes transceiver configuration extraction, firmware analysis of radio stacks, baseband protocol analysis, and evaluation of frequency hopping, encryption, and pairing mechanisms as implemented in hardware.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to hardware-level radio transceiver security

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands common wireless transceiver architectures and their security properties
evidence: Can describe common wireless transceiver architectures (SoC-integrated, external module, discrete)
Understands the difference between baseband/PHY and protocol-level security assessment
Aware of common radio standards (BLE, Zigbee, LoRa, Sub-GHz) and their hardware implementations

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Analyzes radio hardware configuration and captures RF traffic under supervision
evidence: Identifies radio transceiver ICs on target PCBs and locates relevant datasheets
Extracts radio configuration registers via debug interface or firmware analysis
Captures and decodes OTA radio traffic using SDR or dedicated sniffers with guidance
Identifies the RF communication protocol stack and key parameters (frequency, modulation, channel hopping)

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses hardware radio security including firmware-level radio stack analysis
evidence: Reverse engineers radio transceiver firmware to assess encryption and authentication implementation
Evaluates pairing and key exchange mechanisms as implemented in device hardware/firmware
Assesses frequency hopping sequence predictability and randomness
Completed hardware radio assessments on 3+ distinct wireless platforms independently

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Assesses proprietary radio implementations; develops custom analysis tooling; mentors team
evidence: Reverse engineers proprietary radio protocols from hardware/firmware analysis
Develops custom radio analysis and injection tooling using SDR platforms
Assesses baseband processor security and radio firmware update mechanisms
Mentors team on radio hardware identification, firmware extraction, and protocol analysis

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Recognized authority on radio hardware security; publishes research; defines methodology
evidence: Published research on radio transceiver vulnerabilities or wireless hardware attacks
Defines the lab's hardware radio assessment methodology
Provides expert consultation on radio hardware security to product development teams
Develops novel hardware-level wireless attack techniques

assessment_methods.description: Assess the radio implementation of a prepared target: identify the transceiver, extract configuration, analyze the protocol stack, and evaluate security mechanisms
Review hardware radio assessment reports for completeness of transceiver analysis and quality of security findings

equipment: Software-defined radio (SDR) platform for RF capture and analysis
BLE 5-capable sniffer (nRF52-based, e.g. Sniffle), or Ubertooth One for BLE 4.x only
RF shielded enclosure for controlled testing
